coefficient_selection: Verified lexicographic training-cost minimum within each same architecture/fold; reviewed roles retained
interpretation: Reused exploratory validation and descriptive empirical thresholds, not blind calibration or nominal predictive coverage
uncertainty_recommendations: Observation uncertainty is not prediction uncertainty. Preserve the printed/pressure-corrected measurement uncertainty and source notes per repeat; shared references, comb/cell calibration and common line structure create dependence.

The saved potential fits contain coefficients and predictions but no Jacobian or covariance. HF fits contain unweighted derivatives for both train and held-out intervals; only the training rows may enter a conditional HF calculation. These derivatives hold the potential fixed, omit potential/HF/calibration cross-covariance and inherited-constant uncertainty, and do not yield a complete-model prediction interval.

A defensible parameter-uncertainty study should rerun the entire accepted potential/HF/calibration estimator in source or connected line/source block bootstrap replicates, with correlation-sensitivity scenarios. Refit calibration and retain start/physical/numerical checks inside each replicate. Fixed inherited constants need separate physical uncertainty propagation when available. No bootstrap/refit is performed here.

Local linear parameter covariance could be studied after reconstructing the full estimator derivative, including potential-dependent wavefunctions, hyperfine coupling, calibration and active constraints. The current alternating accepted estimator is not a single already-saved joint raw likelihood; a conditional inverse HF Hessian cannot substitute for its full covariance.

Model discrepancy and parameter sensitivity must be reported separately. Whole-band/source residual biases and optimizer-start changes can dominate MHz-scale errors even when a routine component RMS is below 0.2 MHz. Empirical error envelopes describe the sampled cases only and never adjust model frequencies.

Formal block conformal or nominal coverage requires a prospective, appropriate exchangeability design with enough independent calibration groups, kept separate from model selection. The reused seven folds overlap and several contain only one source block. A leave-one-connected-block-out maximum check here is descriptive, not a coverage guarantee or 95% interval.

A new independent measurement of an archived transition tests reproducibility against a new measurement; it does not establish prediction of a previously unseen transition. Freeze all point predictions, empirical widths, fixed accuracy thresholds and provenance before inspecting new-paper outcomes.

absolute_fold_overlap.interpretation: The union count only inventories overlap. Residuals from differently trained fits are never pooled as independent samples.

intraline_fold_overlap.interpretation: The union count only inventories overlap. Residuals from differently trained fits are never pooled as independent samples.

empirical_envelope.recipe: M is largest absolute repeat-level prediction error of training-selected fits; S is largest same-fold/same-identity prediction difference to another accepted numerical start. Routine uses future cohort only; stress takes maxima across future and seven separate folds. Widths are fixed before the new-paper outcomes, not estimated confidence levels.
limitations: Reused architecture-selection data
Overlapping and nonexchangeable folds
Tiny source/band blocks
Two numerical continuations do not define a parameter distribution
A new high-J band can exceed all historical errors
No correction to any point prediction
